relation_reviews.evidence_and_limit: DBI Gabrieli and Merulo corroborate concurrent San Marco organ posts from 1566 to 1584. Joint performance of any specific piece is not thereby proven. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/andrea-gabrieli_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

Mozarteum identifies Salieri, Mozart and Cornetti as contributors to the 1785 joint canzone on Da Ponte's words: genuine multi-author composition. [Fonte](https://dme.mozarteum.at/DME/libredition/single.php?end=1&idwnma=5587&line=0&v=390)

Source in record seems too weak to infer a specific shared undertaking from Liszt's appreciation and Borodin's collaborative Paraphrases. Check letters/concert programmes before calling a collaboration. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/aleksandr-porfir-evic-borodin_%28Enciclopedia-Italiana%29/)

Liszt's advocacy and the 1877 Weimar premiere of Samson et Dalila give an identifiable professional support relation, not co-composition; direct documentary role could be specified. [Fonte](https://pad.philharmoniedeparis.fr/0780746-samson-et-dalila-de-camille-saint-saens.aspx?_lg=fr-FR)

Personal and professional acquaintance in Mannheim is distinct from composition or conducting a work together. Keep as contact if taxonomy permits, not undifferentiated collaboration. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/wolfgang-amadeus-mozart_%28Enciclopedia-Italiana%29/)

The Weber Gesamtausgabe lists Weber and Meyerbeer among the 1810 founding circle, with extant statutes and correspondence on mutual publicity of works. [Fonte](https://weber-gesamtausgabe.de/de/A080146.html)
The Société Camille Saint-Saëns dates Viardot's costumed private performance of act II as Dalila at Croissy to 20 August 1874. [Fonte](https://camille-saint-saens.org/1868-1874/)

Treccani identifies Malipiero, Casella and D'Annunzio in the 1923 foundation of Corporazione delle nuove musiche. Record institution-making, not jointly composed music. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/gian-francesco-malipiero/)

DBI Casella lists Respighi among founders of the Società nazionale di musica and the inaugural concert on 16 March 1917. A separate short Treccani Roma notice gives 1915: preserve conflicting dating source rather than silently overwrite. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/alfredo-casella_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

Joint Roman musical milieu and institutional setting are plausible; verify a specifically named performance by Corelli of Scarlatti before treating it as individual performing collaboration. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/arcangelo-corelli_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

Schoenberg Center reproduces and dates Strauss recommendation letters of 16 April and 5 November 1902, with the Stern Conservatory position linked to the latter. [Fonte](https://schoenberg.at/en/newsblog/new-aquisition-letter-from-richard-strauss)

Mahler conducting Zemlinsky's Es war einmal in Vienna in 1900 constitutes actual conductor-composer work, subject to checking a theater programme/catalogue. [Fonte](https://www.mahlerfoundation.org/mahler/contemporaries/alexander-von-zemlinsky/)

Britten Pears Arts explicitly states The Prodigal Son was dedicated to Shostakovich and Shostakovich's Symphony 14 in return to Britten. This is reciprocal dedication, not joint composition. [Fonte](https://www.brittenpearsarts.org/music/the-prodigal-son)

Digital letters of 1909 document Busoni's piano transcription of op.11 no.2 and communication with Breitkopf & Härtel; editorial mediation and arrangement documented. [Fonte](https://busoni-nachlass.org/de/Korrespondenz/E010001/D0100015.html)

DBI Casella cites the performance of Petrouchka with Stravinsky present and further Italian promotion; a precise performance may replace a vague association. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/alfredo-casella_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

The CNM presented works of Bartók, but organizational credit and the specific role of Casella warrant differentiation. Do not infer co-production of Bartók's music. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/mario-labroca_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

The CNM introduced works by Hindemith in Italy; specify organization-versus-individual promotion and dates if possible. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/mario-labroca_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

Encounter in the Rome/Naples milieu does not itself prove participation in a shared work. Classify as contact rather than generic collaboration unless event-specific joint documentation is found. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/georg-friedrich-handel_%28Enciclopedia-Italiana%29/)

Dvořák's official site details meeting in Prague in early 1888, score exchange (Tchaikovsky Suite 3; Dvořák Symphony 7) and Tchaikovsky's invitation leading to Dvořák's 1890 Russia concerts. [Fonte](https://www.antonin-dvorak.cz/en/index-of-names/tchaikovsky-peter-ilyich-1840-1893/)

Michael Kelly's late reminiscence is a single remembered private quartet with Haydn, Dittersdorf, Mozart, Vanhal. Preserve testimonial caution, not stable ensemble or proof of frequent joint projects. [Fonte](https://wanhal.org/news/after-the-party-wanhal-storace-and-his-collection-of-original-keyboard-music-2/)

Same memorial episode as preceding record; no independent second source, no durable ensemble. Two graph edges are different pairs but rely on one testimonial event. [Fonte](https://wanhal.org/news/after-the-party-wanhal-storace-and-his-collection-of-original-keyboard-music-2/)

A general Beethoven-Haus image/archive reference alone was not independently checked for the compound claims about Bonn university, court orchestra and Vienna in 1802. Keep source and request more specific documentation. [Fonte](https://www.beethoven.de/en/media/view/5068360102445056/scan/0)

Schoenberg Center identifies home footage of the personal relationship in California; friendship is distinct from stylistic influence or composition in common. [Fonte](https://schoenberg.at/en/newsblog/george-gershwin-films-arnold-schoenberg)

Mahler Foundation reports Berg present at Essen rehearsals in 1906 and dinner with the composer, but this remains a secondary reconstruction: one event, not an ongoing cooperation. [Fonte](https://mahlerfoundation.org/mahler/contemporaries/julius-buths/)

Historic biographical account places Gabrieli in contact with Lasso in Munich; an encounter does not entail collaboration in composition or a teacher-student relationship. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/andrea-e-giovanni-gabrieli_%28Storia-della-civilta-europea-a-cura-di-Umberto-Eco%29/)

Bruckner's dedication of Symphony 3 to Wagner documents personal and professional recognition; record that precisely, not a shared work or sustained patronage. [Fonte](https://www.brucknerjournal.com/Issues/ewExternalFiles/18i%20A4.pdf)

Specialist history reports Debussy and Stravinsky playing the Sacre reduction four hands on 9 June 1912. Confirm date against diary or correspondence before treating it as primary document. [Fonte](https://publishing.cdlib.org/ucpressebooks/public/book/stravinsky-and-the-rite-of-spring.html)

A university thesis reconstructs Gershwin's 1928 Vienna encounter with Berg and acquisition of interest in Berg's work: reception/meeting, not demonstrable joint composition. [Fonte](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/4c0188rh)

IMSLP work page establishes La resurrezione HWV 47 but is not enough, by itself, to certify Corelli's actual function at the 1708 premiere. Require a named performance history / documentary source. [Fonte](https://imslp.org/wiki/La_Resurrezione%2C_HWV_47_%28Handel%2C_George_Frideric%29)

DBI Sivori explicitly dates Paris June 1876 and notes Verdi engaging Sivori as first violin in performance of his string quartet in E minor. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/camillo-ernesto-sivori_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

Beethoven-Haus states the 1782 Nine Variations WoO63 were written as Neefe's pupil and that Neefe arranged publication with Götz in Mannheim. [Fonte](https://www.beethoven.de/en/work/view/5175547688648704/Nine%20Variations%20on%20a%20march%20by%20Ernst%20Christoph%20Dressler%20for%20piano%20%26%2340%3BC%20minor%26%2341%3B%20WoO%2063)

Text-setting and correspondence connect Goethe and Zelter; artistic cooperation through Goethe poems should be distinguished from mere friendship. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/karl-friedrich-zelter_%28Enciclopedia-Italiana%29/)

BnF manuscript catalogue says first 20 pages of Khamma are in Debussy's hand and the remainder in Koechlin's, identifying the latter as orchestrator. Beware false co-authorship of the original score. [Fonte](https://catalogue.bnf.fr/ark:/12148/cb42939285v)

Treccani attributes close friendship and shared aesthetic initiatives. Cooperation has no inherent causal direction from Cui to Balakirev; preserve source-target fields yet note reciprocal relation. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/milij-alekseevic-balakirev_%28Enciclopedia-Italiana%29/)

Chicago Symphony credits Reiner and Szigeti in advocating the Koussevitzky commission for Bartók's Concerto for Orchestra; documentary particulars need checking directly from foundation papers. [Fonte](https://chicagosymphony.org/inside-the-music/article/21955/bartok-in-chicago)

Treccani lists Galuppi among notable opera buffa composers; this is a genre membership and transformation relation, not an individual genealogical parent-child link. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/opera/)

Treccani discusses Scarlatti's contribution to aria-recitativo and closed-number conventions at the beginning of the 18th century. Avoid representing him as sole founder of opera seria. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/opera_%28Enciclopedia-dei-ragazzi%29/)

Treccani expressly identifies Auber's La muette de Portici, premiered 29 February 1828, as first grand-opéra in its narrative; not all historical authors agree on hard origins. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/il-grand-opera_%28Storia-della-civilta-europea-a-cura-di-Umberto-Eco%29/)

Auber composed important works in the French opéra-comique tradition, which is not reducible to invariably comic plots; evidence and source are biographical. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/daniel-francois-esprit-auber/)

The Arnold Schönberg Center dates his public explanation of the twelve-tone method in February 1923; record ideation, not a claim that first every twelve-tone composition was produced in that year. [Fonte](https://schoenberg.at/en/schoenberghaus/schoenberg-and-moedling)

Berg adapted twelve-tone technique in works including Lyric Suite, but the work is not an undifferentiated demonstration of total serialization. Specific passages/works required. [Fonte](https://resources.ircam.fr/en/composer/alban-berg/biography)
Webern's twelve-tone technique grows from 1925, distinct from postwar integral serialism; avoid anachronistically conflating them. [Fonte](https://brahms.ircam.fr/en/composer/anton-webern/workcourse)

Official Britten Pears Arts identifies The Turn of the Screw (1954) as a chamber opera scored for six singers and small orchestra. [Fonte](https://www.brittenpearsarts.org/music/the-turn-of-the-screw)

Official Britten Pears Arts describes Owen Wingrave as Britten's only opera written directly for television, screened 16 May 1971 on BBC2. [Fonte](https://www.brittenpearsarts.org/music/owen-wingrave)

Gesualdo's late madrigal books evidence expressive chromatic writing; genre node -> composer should not be mistaken for an actual artist-to-artist genealogy. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/carlo-gesualdo_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

Monteverdi develops madrigal practice from polyphony toward seconda pratica and concertato; genre membership versus chronological lineage must remain distinct. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/claudio-monteverdi_%28Enciclopedia-Italiana%29/)

Already individually reviewed in Audit qualità 02: the term cromatici refers primarily to black-note notation; DO NOT infer modern chromatic harmony solely from the title. No redundant new claim here. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/cipriano-de-rore_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

Already individually reviewed in Audit qualità 02: Musica nova contains both Italian madrigals and Latin motets, not one homogeneous genre. No repetition of collational work. [Fonte](https://imslp.org/wiki/Musica_nova_%28Willaert%2C_Adrian%29)

DBI Barbara Strozzi confirms the 1644 first book and that Giulio Strozzi authored its poetic texts; historically concrete late madrigal production. [Fonte](https://www.treccani.it/enciclopedia/barbara-strozzi_%28Dizionario-Biografico%29/)

Opéra-Comique directly identifies Mignon as opéra-comique in three acts premiered 17 November 1866; belonging to this genre not equivalent to exclusively comic subject matter. [Fonte](https://www.opera-comique.com/en/shows/mignon)

limits: Questo file ricostruisce fedelmente ID, gradi ed estremi del rapporto Audit 16; non sostituisce le descrizioni integrali nel rapporto.
Gli interventi editoriali rimangono proposte separate dai cambi applicati in fase cumulativa.
